newsitem.title: UK: Major says he wants May 1 British election-sources.
newsitem.headline: Major says he wants May 1 British election-sources.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major has told ministerial colleagues that his favoured date for an election is May 1, Conservative Party sources said on Monday.
They said Major reaffirmed the date at the start of a cabinet meeting at his official country house, Chequers, held to consider what pledges to include in the party's election manifesto.
Major says he wants May 1 British election- =2
The Conservatives are currently almost 20 percentage points behind the opposition Labour Party in the opinion polls.
Major must hold an election by May 22, but there has been recent press speculation that he might appeal to the voters in April or even March.
A spokeswoman at Conservative headquarters said earlier that the party would move the writ for a by-election in Wirral South near Liverpool by next Monday.

The by-election would then be held in late February or early March, providing a crucial snapshot of voter opinion ahead of the nationwide clash of the parties. If the Conservatives lose the seat, they will again be in a minority in the House of Commons.
